source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ / Climate Resilient Orange Growing Technique", Nov 2018, 23pp
text:
The guide includes a seasonal growing calendar (ប្រតិទិនដាំដុះ) showing when key activities - land preparation, weeding, fertilizing, pest and disease control, and harvest - normally fall across the year, so farmers can plan labor and inputs in advance rather than reacting late to each stage.

For harvest, the source notes that farmers can expect to begin picking a portion of the crop (around 30 percent of flowers/fruit having set) starting from around the 11th month after major flowering through to the 2nd month of the following cycle, reflecting the fact that Pursat orange trees do not ripen all their fruit at exactly the same time and harvest is typically done in rounds.
